reviewer: OpenAI Codex root, independent of initial Codacy triage
scope: All 76 production/documentation/script proposed false positives; 239 test proposals remain outside this independent review
method: Read the actual current implementations, callers and protection helpers for each listed issue. Checked local configuration authority, path confinement, readonly object traversal, literal VM source with timeout, numeric exactness and caught async propagation. Source bindings below capture the reviewed files. Second pass inspected dispatch tables and their kind/permission guards, browser worker ownership and termination, native Request normalization, executor origin allowlist, operator-owned webhook configuration, provider label/cursor/test fixtures, and offline subprocess blocking. No runtime input was identified as arbitrary executable source or an untrusted server network target at these specific sinks.
limitations: No Codacy platform state was changed. These are reviewed classifications, not code fixes or a fresh scan.
Local operator-controlled configuration is trusted; this review does not claim protection against a compromised process or operating-system account.
Viewer bot API origin is operator configurable; the runtime trusted-host restriction applies to the Core API only. Neither URL is selected by chat contents.

decisions.rationale: loadEnv uses the fixed module-relative ../.env. resolveSecretFiles accepts only operator process-environment *_FILE entries from FILE_BACKED_SECRETS, resolves them, requires a regular file <=16KiB and a single nonempty line. Remote request bodies cannot select the file.

Core URL comes from TELEGRAM_VIEWER_CORE_URL through requireTrustedServiceUrl (HTTPS or trusted internal HTTP hosts). Resource is config or CORE_RESOURCES; query uses URL.searchParams. Telegram URL comes from operator env/default api.telegram.org, token grammar is checked, methods are a fixed three-item allowlist. User chat content stays in JSON body.
reviewNode only READS a bounded path inside an authorized object. Each segment must be an own property and pass protectedKey redaction; node=node[key] never writes a prototype property.

Prometheus origin is operator PROMETHEUS_URL, validated HTTPS (HTTP only loopback) without credentials/fragment; query is added with URLSearchParams, redirect:error and 15s timeout. The 805306368 byte threshold is exactly representable as a JavaScript integer.

live.token !== token compares object IDENTITY of an in-process frozen observation capability, not secret strings. The in-process live registry and current epoch verify invalidation authority; constant-time string comparison would not preserve this semantic.

Compiled pattern is length-limited to150 and nested quantifiers are rejected. Actual filtering runs safeRegexTest in a VM with100ms CPU timeout on bounded text; compilation itself does not match hostile input. Static executable VM source never contains user text.

Writes require process-lock ownership and generation barrier; exclusiveWrite uses wx/0600. Reported sink is part of this intended local persistence boundary, not a request-supplied filename.

section is selected only from the literal requiredSections array Risk/Evidence/Compensating controls/Exit criteria. Document content is matched text, not regex source.

URL is built against literal https://api.github.com/ from individually encodeURIComponent-encoded pathSegments; query uses URLSearchParams. Encoded segments cannot replace the origin; the script is an operator/CI governance reader.
The flagged API Secret/Password/Token strings are human-readable credential-field LABELS in a metadata dictionary. They are returned as labels, never used as authentication values.
token=None is a pagination cursor sentinel when advancing orders to triggers. It represents absence of a provider continuation token, not a hardcoded password.

Regex source uses version from checked-in package.json under repository-maintainer control. Semantic Version syntax is checked and dots are escaped; no remote input reaches this build-only checker. Invalid source metadata can fail CI and must not be treated as public runtime input.

selection validates query kind with KINDS.includes against six literals before handlers[page.kind] is invoked. Arbitrary/prototype keys are rejected before dispatch.

baseUrl is internalExecutorOrigin(process.env.EXCHANGE_EXECUTOR_URL); endpoints are internal literal /v1 operations selected by adapter methods. External trading payload is cloned into JSON body and cannot choose the executor origin.

subprocess import exists solely so the offline audit blocker can patch subprocess.Popen alongside sockets/HTTP. It prevents process launches during metadata enumeration; no command is executed by this import.

Browser fetch is not a server-side network capability. Current helper now normalizes a native Request before adding credentials, checks the normalized URL against dashboard origin, and sends the same Request with redirects rejected. Mutable URL coercion and shadowed Request.url regressions pass in the integrated 316-test frontend suite. This defense hardening is distinct from classification of the server-side SSRF rule.

RESOURCE_VALIDATORS is a fixed table. Creating resources rejects kinds outside RESOURCE_KINDS; persisted resource kind is reused on update. The input is configuration data for local validator functions, not dynamically compiled executable code.
The reported token === slash branch compares a parsed public trading-pair lexical token against the literal / delimiter. It is not an authentication token or secret comparison.
defaultAt traverses defaults by READ only, requiring Object.hasOwn(current, part) before current=current[part]. There is no assignment into the object or its prototype.

Pattern is deliberately user-selected regex. Work runs in a dedicated Worker with200-character/5000-entry/1MB limits. Owner use-log-search terminates worker after500ms and on completion/unmount, bounding catastrophic matching outside the UI thread.
